segments.text: A foundational warm up. Find the plane through the point two, minus one, three with normal i plus two j minus two k, and its perpendicular distance from the origin.
Apply the point normal form. One times x minus two, plus two times y plus one, minus two times z minus three, equals zero.
Expanding and collecting terms gives the plane x plus two y minus two z plus six equals zero.
For the distance of the origin, feed zero, zero, zero into the plane expression and divide by the length of the normal, root nine, which is three.
That gives six over three, which is two units.

The same answer falls out of the normal form. Dividing the plane by the size of the normal and flipping signs so the right side is non negative gives r dot n hat equals two, with n hat a unit vector — confirming the origin distance is two.
The through line here: the plane form came straight from the normal, and the distance divided by the normal's length. Identify the normal first and the rest follows.
This is the classic sine trap. Find the angle between a given line and the plane three x minus six y plus two z equals seven.
The line's direction is two, minus one, two, and the plane's normal is three, minus six, two.
The dot product is two times three, plus minus one times minus six, plus two times two — that is six plus six plus four, equals sixteen.
The magnitude of the direction is three, and of the normal is seven.
Because this is a line and a plane, we use sine, not cosine. Sin phi is sixteen over twenty one, so phi is the inverse sine of sixteen over twenty one.

<whisper>Here is the trap</whisper>. Sixteen over twenty one is the cosine of the angle the line makes with the normal. A student who writes inverse cosine has reported the angle with the normal, not the plane — off by exactly ninety degrees. Whenever a line meets a plane, reach for sine.

And there is a built in safeguard: sin phi is sixteen over twenty one, which is less than one, exactly as any genuine sine must be. Had we divided by only one magnitude, the result would have exceeded one, instantly flagging the slip.

A multi concept problem using the family shortcut. Find the plane through the line of intersection of x plus y plus z equals six and two x plus three y plus four z plus five equals zero, passing through one, one, one.
Write the family: x plus y plus z minus six, plus lambda times two x plus three y plus four z plus five, equals zero.
Impose the point one, one, one by substituting it in. The first bracket becomes three minus six, and the second becomes fourteen.
So minus three plus fourteen lambda equals zero, giving lambda equal to three over fourteen.
Substitute this lambda back and clear the fraction by multiplying through by fourteen.
Collecting terms gives the plane twenty x plus twenty three y plus twenty six z minus sixty nine equals zero. Check: at one, one, one, that sums to zero.

The whole problem collapsed to one linear equation in lambda. Because the family already encodes through the intersection line, a single point condition fully determined the plane — no simultaneous equations, no parametrisation.

An advanced family problem. Find the plane through the line of intersection of two x plus y minus z equals three and x minus y plus two z equals one, that is perpendicular to the plane three x plus two y plus z equals zero.
Write the family, two x plus y minus z minus three, plus lambda times x minus y plus two z minus one. Its normal is two plus lambda, one minus lambda, minus one plus two lambda.
Perpendicular to the plane three x plus two y plus z means the family's normal dotted with three, two, one equals zero.
Expanding: three times two plus lambda, plus two times one minus lambda, plus one times minus one plus two lambda. This simplifies to seven plus three lambda equals zero.
So lambda equals minus seven thirds.

Substituting and clearing the fraction gives the plane x minus ten y plus seventeen z plus two equals zero. Its normal one, minus ten, seventeen dots with three, two, one to give zero — genuinely perpendicular.

The advanced idea: perpendicular to a plane became a single dot product condition on the family normal. One condition yields exactly one plane, because the family carries a single free parameter; two conditions would over determine the pencil.
Let's close the plane subtopic by locking in the traps examiners rely on.
First and biggest: the line plane angle is the complement of the line normal angle, so it uses sine. Writing cosine reports the angle with the normal, off by ninety degrees.
Second, in the point normal form, the coefficients a, b, c are the normal, while x one, y one, z one is the point — never the reverse. Swapping them builds the wrong plane entirely.
Third, the normal form r dot n hat equals p gives p as the distance from the origin only if n hat is a genuine unit vector. If you forgot to normalise, p is not the distance.

Fourth, before using the parallel plane distance, scale both planes so their normals are identical. Two x minus y plus two z equals six and four x minus two y plus four z equals nine must first be matched, or the constants are not comparable.

Fifth, in family problems you never need the intersection line. Write P one plus lambda P two equals zero and impose the single extra condition. And remember the form can never reproduce P two itself.

The one pro tip that ties it together: almost every plane question reduces to find the normal. Forms come from a normal, the plane to plane angle is the normal to normal angle, and distance divides by the normal's length. Identify the normal first and the rest follows.

<curious>Here is a reassuring secret about this whole subtopic</curious> — almost every shortest, nearest, foot, or image question is the same physical act: stand at a point off to one side, and drop a perpendicular onto a line or a plane.
Three things appear the instant you do it. The foot F, where the perpendicular lands; the distance, the length P F of that perpendicular; and the image P dash, the mirror reflection of P.
These are not three separate topics; they are three readings of one drawing. Find the foot and you immediately get the distance, which is the size of P F, and the image.
The image formula is beautifully simple. Because the foot F is the midpoint of P and its reflection, the image is twice the foot minus the point.
So which of the three a question asks for is almost cosmetic. A dozen differently worded problems collapse to one routine, so your practice compounds very quickly.
And the only thing that differs between the line case and the plane case is how you locate the foot. Everything downstream of the foot — distance and image — is identical.

One clean boundary case: if the point already lies on the line or plane, the distance is zero, the foot is the point itself, and the image coincides with it. Every formula returns these degenerate answers automatically, so no special casing is needed.
Take a line, r equals a plus lambda b. From the known point a on the line, draw the arrow A P to your external point. Now split that arrow into two parts.
Here is the decomposition. One part runs along the line, the other sticks straight out perpendicular to it. The along part carries you to the foot; the out part is the distance.
The dot product hands you the shadow along the line. The along piece has length equal to the projection of A P onto the direction, so sliding that far from a lands you exactly at the foot.
So the foot parameter lambda nought is A P dot b over the size of b squared, and the foot is a plus lambda nought times b.
The cross product hands you the height above the line. The cross of A P with b already strips out the along component and keeps only the perpendicular part, scaled by the size of b.
So the perpendicular distance is the size of A P cross b, divided by the size of b — we divide by b just once, because the cross product already carries one factor of it.
So the dot and the cross are not two unrelated formulas. They are the two legs of one right angled decomposition of the arrow A P: the dot product for the foot, the cross product for the gap.

A plane is even friendlier than a line, because the perpendicular direction is handed to you for free — it is the plane's normal. So from the point, you simply step along the normal until you hit the plane.
Here is the picture. There is nothing to decompose and no angle to chase — the whole job is how many normals away is the plane. That count is a single number we call t.
How far to step is fixed by forcing the landing point to satisfy the plane equation, which gives t equal to the plane expression at the point, over the size of the normal squared.
Step t along the normal to reach the foot, and twice as far, two t, to reach the image. Note the minus sign — the correcting step moves the point toward the plane.
And the distance is simply the size of t times the length of the normal, which reduces to the familiar plane expression over the length of the normal.

Images are worth more than they first appear. By a classic reflection principle, the shortest path from A to B that must first touch a surface is found by reflecting one point across it: the straight segment to the image gives the shortest total path.

Recognising this asymmetry up front stops students from over engineering. For a plane you never resolve anything and never chase an angle — you just count normals. The plane case is genuinely easier than the line case.
A board level problem asking for all three at once. Drop the point two, four, one onto the given line, and find the foot, the distance and the image.
Read off a as one, two, three and b as one, minus one, one, so the size of b squared is three. The vector A P, point minus a, is one, two, minus two.
The foot parameter is A P dot b over three, that is one minus two minus two over three, which is minus one. So the foot is a minus b, the point zero, three, two.
For the distance, A P cross b is zero, minus three, minus three, with magnitude root eighteen. Dividing by root three gives the distance, root six.
And the image is twice the foot minus the point: minus two, two, three.

Always run the perpendicularity check. The vector P F is minus two, minus one, one, and its dot with b is minus two plus one plus one, which is zero. Genuinely perpendicular — this one line catches almost every slip in lambda nought.
The template for all such problems: compute lambda nought first. It turns the abstract somewhere on the line into the concrete foot, after which the distance and the image are trivial.
A speed trap that hinges entirely on the denominator. Find the distance of the point one, zero, two from the line through three, one, one with direction two, two, one.
The vector A P, point minus the line's point, is minus two, minus one, one, and the direction b is two, two, one.
The cross product A P with b comes out minus three, four, minus two.
Its magnitude is root nine plus sixteen plus four, which is root twenty nine, and the size of b is three.
So the distance is root twenty nine over three.

<whisper>Here is the trap</whisper> — the denominator is the size of b, three, not b squared, nine, and certainly not missing. The cross product already contains one factor of the size of b, so you divide by exactly one more.

A reliable way to never misremember: dimensionally, the cross product behaves like length times the size of b, so to recover a pure length you cancel exactly one power of the size of b. One division, never two.
A multi concept problem, three answers from one number. Find the foot, distance and image of the point four, one, three in the plane x minus two y plus two z minus five equals zero.
The normal is one, minus two, two, so the size of the normal squared is nine.
Compute t: the plane expression at the point is four minus two plus six minus five, which is three, over nine — so t is one third.
The foot is the point minus one third times the normal, which is eleven thirds, five thirds, seven thirds.
The distance is the size of t times the length of the normal, one third times three, which is one unit.
And the image is the point minus two thirds times the normal, which is ten thirds, seven thirds, five thirds. Three answers, all from the single number t.

A neat sign check: t is positive, so the point sits on the positive side of the plane, where the expression is bigger than zero. The correcting step, minus t times the normal, therefore moves the point toward the plane — exactly as it must.

aur image hai twice the foot minus the point: minus two, two, three.

hamesha perpendicularity check kijiye. vector P F hai minus two, minus one, one, aur uska b ke saath dot hai minus two plus one plus one, jo zero hai. sachmuch perpendicular — ye ek line lambda nought ki lagbhag har galti pakad leti hai.

ek speed trap jo poori tarah denominator par tika hai. point one, zero, two ki us line se distance nikaaliye jo three, one, one se guzarti hai, direction two, two, one ke saath.
Vector A P, point minus line ka point, hai minus two, minus one, one, aur direction b hai two, two, one.

iska magnitude hai root nau plus solah plus chaar, yaani root untees, aur b ka size teen hai.
to distance hai root untees over teen.
yahaan trap hai — denominator hai b ka size, teen, b ka square nau nahin, aur bilkul gayab nahin. cross product pehle hi b ke size ka ek factor rakhta hai, to aap bas ek aur se divide karte hain.

kabhi na bhoolne ka reliable tareeka: dimensionally, cross product length times b ke size jaisa behave karta hai, to pure length paane ke liye aap b ke size ki theek ek power cancel karte hain. ek division, kabhi do nahin.
ek multi concept problem, ek number se teen answers. point four, one, three ka plane x minus two y plus two z minus five equals zero mein foot, distance aur image nikaaliye.

aur image hai point minus two thirds times normal, yaani ten thirds, seven thirds, five thirds. teen answers, sab single number t se.

ek saaf sign check: t positive hai, to point plane ke positive side par baitha hai, jahan expression zero se bada hai. correcting step, minus t times normal, isliye point ko plane ki taraf le jata hai — theek jaisa hona chahiye.

Projection: intersect the plane with the plane through the line perpendicular to it.

Now the decisive second test: substitute a point of the line into the plane.
$\vec b\cdot\vec n=0$ fixes orientation only — never declare lies-in without the point test.
One test fixes orientation, the other fixes position — you need both.

The slips that cost configuration marks

segments.text: An advanced problem, but the routine is unchanged. Find the image of the point one, six, three in the given line.
Read a as zero, one, two and b as one, two, three, so the size of b squared is fourteen. The vector A P is one, five, one.
The foot parameter is A P dot b over fourteen, that is one plus ten plus three over fourteen, which is fourteen over fourteen, equal to one.
So the foot is a plus b, the point one, three, five.
And the image is twice the foot minus the point: one, zero, seven.

Verify two ways. The vector P F dotted with b is zero, confirming perpendicularity, and the midpoint of P and P dash is one, three, five, which is exactly the foot. The clean integer lambda nought equal to one is the hallmark of a well posed reflection problem.
That invariance is the point of practising on clean numbers first. When lambda nought is a messy fraction instead of one, the procedure does not change one bit — only the arithmetic does.
Let's lock in the traps around feet, distances and images before we move to the final subtopic.
First, the point line distance divides by the size of b exactly once. The cross product already carries one factor of it, so dividing by the size of b squared is the classic over division.
Second, do not report the foot as the image. The image is twice the foot minus the point; the foot is only the midpoint of the point and its image. Memorise it as twice the foot minus the point.

Third, do not confuse t with the distance. The parameter t divides by the size of the normal squared, while the distance divides by the size of the normal. They differ by exactly one factor of the normal's length.
Fourth, step the normal the right way — the foot is the point minus t times the normal, with a minus. And that step is a vector scaled by t, not t added to each coordinate separately.

The headline pro tip: never solve a distance, foot and image set separately. Find the foot first; the distance is the size of P F and the image is twice the foot minus the point. And on the line case, always run the one line perpendicularity check — it exposes a wrong foot instantly.

And a powerful pro tip: if a problem asks for the minimum total distance of a path that must touch a surface, reflect one endpoint across it and join to the other with a straight segment. The segment's length is the answer, and its crossing point is the optimal contact.
By now you can describe lines and planes separately. The real exam questions ask how they fit together, and a line and a plane can do exactly three things.

The line can pierce the plane at a single point — the generic case; it can lie flat inside the plane, every point on it; or it can run parallel and never touch. Recognising which one you face is half the battle.

The deciding quantity is the dot product of the line's direction with the plane's normal. If it is non zero, the line is not perpendicular to the normal, so it must cross — one clean intersection point.
If the dot product is zero, the line is perpendicular to the normal, hence parallel to the surface. But now a second test decides between lies in and merely parallel.

This is the crucial point. The dot product being zero is necessary but never sufficient for a line to lie in a plane. A railway track running alongside a wall is parallel to it, yet clearly not painted on the wall. You must test a point.

So pick any point of the line and check whether it satisfies the plane. On the plane means the whole line lies in it; off the plane means strictly parallel. One condition fixes orientation, the other fixes position.
And when the line does cross, finding the point is mechanical: write the moving parametric point, substitute it into the plane equation, and solve the single linear equation for lambda.
Often you must produce the plane that contains given data. The recipe is always the same — find the normal, then use a point — and the normal always comes from a cross product.
Here is the idea for a line and an external point. The line's direction and the vector from the line to the point both lie in the plane, so their cross product is the normal.
If you have two intersecting lines, their two directions both lie in the plane, so the normal is their cross product.
If you have a line and an external point, the direction and the vector from the line to the point both lie in the plane, so the normal is their cross product.
And for two parallel lines, the shared direction and the vector joining them lie in the plane, giving the normal as their cross product. Same idea every time.
One limit to respect: a plane through two lines only exists if those lines are coplanar, that is, intersecting or parallel. Skew lines do not lie in any common plane, so there is nothing to find.
Once you have the normal, finish with the point normal form through any one known point. Two in plane vectors, one cross product, then point normal — that is the entire construction.
Two intersecting planes make a pair of valley angles, and there are two planes that bisect them — exactly like the two angle bisectors of two crossing lines in the plane.
Here they are in cross section. A point lies on a bisector exactly when it is equidistant from the two planes, and the two bisectors always come out mutually perpendicular.
To get them, write each distance with its sign and set them equal, with a plus or minus for the two bisectors. You normalise each plane by the length of its normal, then equate.
So the bisector planes are the first plane over the size of its normal equals plus or minus the second plane over the size of its normal. Each sign gives one bisector.

Put lambda equal to minus one back into the parametric point to get one, zero, one.

sections.title: The section formula: internal, external, midpoint & related topics

board_events.text: The section formula
Point R divides the join of $A(\vec a)$ and $B(\vec b)$ in ratio $m : n$.
Internal ADDS; external SUBTRACTS, and the denominators differ too.
External division lands R outside the segment, beyond A or B.

board_events.caption: R splits segment AB internally in the ratio m to n.

board_events.text: Proof: the internal section formula
R divides A B internally in ratio $m : n$, so $AR : RB = m : n$.
Same direction along the segment gives $n\,\vec{AR} = m\,\vec{RB}$.
Write segments head minus tail: $\vec{AR} = \vec r - \vec a$, $\vec{RB} = \vec b - \vec r$.

board_events.latex: n(\vec r - \vec a) = m(\vec b - \vec r)
(m + n)\,\vec r = m\vec b + n\vec a

board_events.text: Since R lies strictly between A and B, $m + n \neq 0$, so dividing is legal.
Example: section formula meets DCs
R divides $A(3,-2,4)$ and $B(8,3,-6)$ internally in $2:3$. Find $\vec{OR}$ and its DCs.

board_events.latex: \vec{OR} = \frac{2\vec b + 3\vec a}{2 + 3} = \frac{2(8\hat i + 3\hat j - 6\hat k) + 3(3\hat i - 2\hat j + 4\hat k)}{5}

board_events.text: Numerator componentwise: i: $16+9=25$; j: $6-6=0$; k: $-12+12=0$.
Magnitude is 5, so the direction cosines are components over 5.
Check: $1^2 + 0^2 + 0^2 = 1$. R lies on the positive x-axis.
Proof: the component formula for the dot product
Claim: $\vec a \cdot \vec b = a_1 b_1 + a_2 b_2 + a_3 b_3$.
Write both vectors in components and use distributivity.
The product expands into nine basis dot products $\hat e_p \cdot \hat e_q$.
Basis rule: $\hat e_p \cdot \hat e_q = 1$ if $p=q$, and $0$ otherwise.
Every cross term with $p \neq q$ dies, leaving only three diagonal terms.

board_events.latex: \vec a \cdot \vec b = a_1 b_1 + a_2 b_2 + a_3 b_3

board_events.text: The whole formula is just the basis rule doing the bookkeeping.
Proof: the determinant formula for the cross product
Expand $\vec a \times \vec b$ by distributivity over nine basis cross products.
Three terms $\hat i \times \hat i$, $\hat j \times \hat j$, $\hat k \times \hat k$ equal $\vec 0$.
The other six pair up via the cyclic rules $\hat i \times \hat j = \hat k$, and so on.

board_events.latex: \vec a \times \vec b = (a_2 b_3 - a_3 b_2)\hat i + (a_3 b_1 - a_1 b_3)\hat j + (a_1 b_2 - a_2 b_1)\hat k

board_events.text: This is exactly the cofactor expansion of the $3\times3$ determinant along its top row.
The determinant's antisymmetry reproduces $\vec a \times \vec b = -\,\vec b \times \vec a$ for free.
So the determinant is not a trick, it is the algebra, packaged neatly.
Formula recap: the whole chapter

board_events.latex: \vec a \cdot \vec b = |\vec a||\vec b|\cos\theta = a_1b_1 + a_2b_2 + a_3b_3
|\vec a \times \vec b| = |\vec a||\vec b|\sin\theta = \text{area of parallelogram}
[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c] = \vec a \cdot (\vec b \times \vec c),\qquad V_{\text{tet}} = \tfrac{1}{6}|[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]|
\vec a \times (\vec b \times \vec c) = (\vec a \cdot \vec c)\vec b - (\vec a \cdot \vec b)\vec c

board_events.text: Three anchors: DC-squares sum to 1; dot = 0 is perpendicular; cross = 0 is parallel.
Cheat sheet: quick decisions
Need a direction only? Build the unit vector, divide by magnitude.
Point dividing a segment? Section formula; internal adds, external subtracts.
Angle between vectors? $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\vec a \cdot \vec b}{|\vec a||\vec b|}$.
Area of triangle? $\tfrac{1}{2}|\vec a \times \vec b|$. Parallelogram? $|\vec a \times \vec b|$.
Perpendicular direction to two vectors? $\pm(\vec a \times \vec b)/|\vec a \times \vec b|$.
Coplanar or volume? Scalar triple product; zero means coplanar.
Simplify $\vec a \times (\vec b \times \vec c)$? Apply back cab immediately.
Know what each zero proves: DC-squares, dot-zero, cross-zero, triple-product-zero.
Distance in 3D is Pythagoras, used twice
First the floor distance to $(x, y, 0)$ is the 2D hypotenuse $\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$.
Then climb the height $z$ and apply Pythagoras again.

board_events.text: Expand double negatives: $2-(-2)=4$, never $0$.
Each difference is squared, so the sign vanishes — the labelling of P and Q does not matter.
Splitting a segment in the ratio m : n
In each coordinate the splitting point is a weighted average — same weights for x, y, z.

board_events.latex: R=\left(\dfrac{m x_{2}+n x_{1}}{m+n},\ \dfrac{m y_{2}+n y_{1}}{m+n},\ \dfrac{m z_{2}+n z_{1}}{m+n}\right)

board_events.text: The heavier weight rides the endpoint you are nearer to.
Weight m multiplies the FAR endpoint $x_2$; n multiplies the near $x_1$.

board_events.text: The midpoint is the sanity check: equal weights land exactly halfway.
Every foundation formula in one place
Distance from x-axis $=\sqrt{y^2+z^2}$; from yz-plane $=|x|$ (cycle for the rest).
Direction and line formulas in one place
Angles and distances between lines, in one place
Pick the form that matches your data — vectors, direction ratios, or Cartesian.
Two constructions, one board
$t$ divides by $|\vec n|^2$; the distance divides by $|\vec n|$ — never interchange them.
Anchor everything on the foot; the image is always $2F-P$ in both cases.
Classify, construct, bisect — on one board

board_events.text: The one-line reminders that save marks
Pythagoras twice; far weight first; negative ratio = outside.
Axis drops one coordinate; plane keeps one.
Cosines on a unit budget; ratios are the recipe, cosines are the dish; standardise then read.
Cross to bridge, dot to project; acute by modulus; zero volume, they meet.
Plane-to-plane cosine, line-to-plane sine; the normal is everything.
Dot for foot, cross for gap; foot is the midpoint, so image = $2F-P$; dot decides; bisect = normalise then $\pm$.

segments.text: The section formula answers a very common question: where does a point R sit if it divides the segment from A to B in a given ratio m to n?
Take A and B with position vectors a and b, and let R split A B in the ratio m to n.
For internal division R lies between them, and its position vector is m times b plus n times a, all over m plus n, and note that m plus n must not be zero.
For external division R lies outside the segment, and the formula switches a sign: m times b minus n times a, over m minus n, with m not equal to n.
And the midpoint is the friendly special case, just a plus b over two, the average of the two ends.
Here is the mnemonic that saves you in the exam, internal adds, external subtracts, and the denominators differ in exactly the same way.

For two general points, build the box that has P and Q as opposite corners. The base diagonal handles two coordinates, and the space diagonal PQ closes the second right triangle.

The point to plane distance, and the family of planes through a line of intersection.

segments.text: Section formula ek bahut common sawaal ka jawab deta hai: point R kahaan baithaga agar wo A se B tak ke segment ko diye hue ratio m to n mein divide kare?
A aur B lijiye position vectors a aur b ke saath, aur R ko A B ko ratio m to n mein split karne dijiye.
Internal division ke liye R unke beech hota hai, aur uska position vector hai m times b plus n times a, whole over m plus n, aur dhyan rahe m plus n zero nahi hona chahiye.
External division ke liye R segment ke bahar hota hai, aur formula ek sign badal deta hai: m times b minus n times a, over m minus n, with m not equal to n.
aur midpoint friendly special case hai, bas a plus b over two, dono ends ka average.
yahaan vo mnemonic hai jo exam mein bacha lega, internal adds, external subtracts, aur denominators bhi exactly usi tarah alag hote hain.

Board par R, A aur B ke beech baith kar segment ko ratio m to n mein kaat raha hai, plug in karte waqt yahi picture rakhiye.
ab ek proof jo saath mein sau doosri problems ki technique bhi dikhata hai, internal section formula derive karna.
R, A B ko internally ratio m to n mein divide karta hai, yaani pieces A R aur R B usi same ratio m to n mein hain.
chunki A R aur R B segment ke saath bilkul same way point karte hain, hum us ratio ko vector equation mein promote kar sakte hain: n times A R equals m times R B.
ab dono segment vectors ko head minus tail likho. A R hai r minus a, aur R B hai b minus r, jahan r, R ka position vector hai.
Substitute karne par milta hai n times the quantity r minus a, equals m times the quantity b minus r.
Expand karke saare r terms ek taraf ikattha karo, aur milta hai m plus n, times r, equals m b plus n a.
Divide kar do aur ye raha: r equals m b plus n a, over m plus n, internal section formula, proven.
aur divide karna perfectly legal hai kyunki R, A aur B ke strictly beech baitha hai, to m plus n kabhi zero nahi ho sakta.
ye J E E Main level problem do ideas ko ek saath stitch karti hai, pehle section formula, phir result ke direction cosines.
R, A ko three, minus two, four par aur B ko eight, three, minus six par, internally ratio two to three mein divide karta hai; chahiye R ka position vector aur uske direction cosines.
Internal formula apply karo: two b plus three a, whole over two plus three, jo five hai, upar dono vectors plug in karke.
Numerator ko component by component solve karo. i-hat ke liye sixteen plus nine hai twenty five; j-hat ke liye six minus six hai zero; k-hat ke liye minus twelve plus twelve hai zero.
to numerator bas twenty five i-hat hai, aur five se divide karne par O R equals five i-hat milta hai, ek clean vector seedha x-axis ke saath.
uski magnitude five hai, to direction cosines har component ko five se divide karke milte hain.
isse milta hai l equals one, m equals zero, n equals zero.
Identity check confirm kar deta hai, one squared plus zero plus zero hai one, aur ye sense banata hai, kyunki R theek positive x-axis par baitha hai.
Prove karte hain ki dot product ka neat component formula sach kyon hai, ye seedhe distributivity se nikalta hai.
Claim ye hai ki a dot b equals a-one b-one plus a-two b-two plus a-three b-three.
donon vectors ko components mein likho, aur yaad rakho dot product sums par distribute karta hai.
donon bracketed expressions ko multiply karne par nine basis dot products bante hain, a ke har i, j, k ko b ke har i, j, k se dot.
ab basis rule lagao: ek basis vector ko khud se dot karo to one, aur alag basis vector se dot karo to zero.
to har cross term, jahan dono basis vectors alag hain, bas mar jata hai, aur sirf teen diagonal terms bachte hain.
vo survivors hain a-one b-one plus a-two b-two plus a-three b-three, bilkul component formula.
poora proof asal mein bas orthonormal basis rule hai jo chupchaap hamare liye bookkeeping kar raha hai.
ab dikhate hain ki cross product ka tidy determinant koi memory trick nahi, balki basis rules ka genuine consequence hai.
a cross b ko distributivity se expand karo, to dono component sums ka product nine basis cross products mein toot jata hai.
un nine mein se teen, i cross i, j cross j, aur k cross k, har ek zero vector hai, to wo nikal jaate hain.
baaki chah cyclic rules ke tahat neatly pair ho jaate hain: i cross j hai k, j cross k hai i, k cross i hai j, aur reverses minus sign carry karte hain.
Survivors ikattha karne par a cross b milta hai, a-two b-three minus a-three b-two along i, plus a-three b-one minus a-one b-three along j, plus a-one b-two minus a-two b-one along k.
aur wo expression theek three by three determinant ka cofactor expansion hai top row ke along.
ek bonus hai, determinant apni last two rows mein antisymmetric hai, to a aur b swap karne par sign apne aap flip hota hai, a cross b equals minus b cross a reproduce karta hai.
to determinant koi shortcut nahi jise blindly rato; ye algebra khud hai, ek neat grid mein packaged.

Components se: magnitude hai squares ke sum ka root, aur unit vector hai vector over uski magnitude.
Direction cosines hamesha square-sum karke one bante hain, aur do points ko join karne wala vector hai head minus tail, b minus a.
Section formula, internal division deta hai m b plus n a over m plus n, aur midpoint bas dono ends ka average hai.
Dot product, dono magnitudes times cosine theta, components ke products ke sum ke equal.
Cross product ki magnitude, dono magnitudes times sine theta, jo parallelogram area hai.
Scalar triple product hai a dotted with b cross c, aur tetrahedron us box ke absolute value ka one sixth hai.
aur vector triple product back cab follow karta hai, a dot c times b, minus a dot b times c.
teen facts se khud ko anchor karo: direction-cosine squares one banate hain, zero dot product matlab perpendicular, aur zero cross product matlab parallel.
aakhir mein, ek decision-style cheat sheet, sawaal ko ek nazar mein tool se match karo.
agar sirf direction chahiye, vector ko uski magnitude se divide karke unit vector banao.
agar koi point segment ko divide karta hai, section formula uthao, internal division adds, external subtracts.
do vectors ke beech angle ke liye, cosine theta hai a dot b over magnitudes ka product.
Triangle ke area ke liye, cross product ki magnitude ka aadha lo; parallelogram ke liye, poori magnitude.
do vectors ke perpendicular direction ke liye, plus or minus cross product over uski magnitude lo.
Coplanarity ya volume ke liye, seedhe scalar triple product par jao; zero matlab vectors coplanar hain.
aur a cross the quantity b cross c ko simplify karne ke liye, turant back cab apply karo, inner cross haath se expand mat karo.
ek master check sab baand deta hai: pakka jaano ki har zero kya prove karta hai, direction-cosine squares, zero dot, zero cross, aur zero triple product, aur aap exam mein confident chal sakte ho.
yahaan vo ek idea hai jo poora distance formula banata hai: three dimensions mein distance bas Pythagoras theorem hai, jo ek ke baad ek do baar lagta hai.
kisi point ki origin se distance nikaalne ke liye, pehle floor par chal kar point x, y, zero tak jaiye. wo flat distance ordinary two D hypotenuse hai, root x squared plus y squared.
ab seedhe upar height z jitna climb kijiye. wo floor distance aur ye vertical climb ek right triangle banate hain, to hum Pythagoras doosri baar lagate hain.
Result behad simple hai: origin se distance hai root x squared plus y squared plus z squared. wo jana-pehchana two term formula bas ek teesra term le aaya.
do general points ke liye, wo box banaiye jiske opposite corners P aur Q hon. base diagonal do coordinates sambhalta hai, aur space diagonal PQ doosra right triangle poora karta hai.
to kisi bhi do points ke beech distance hai har coordinate ke squared difference ke sum ka root. yahi master distance formula hai.
ek warning jo chupke se marks churati hai — jab koi coordinate negative ho, double negative ko dhyan se expand kijiye. two minus negative two chaar hai, zero nahi.
dhyan dijiye har difference square hota hai, to uska sign gayab ho jata hai. matlab isse fark nahi padta aap kise P kahte hain aur kise Q — distance dono tarah se same aati hai.
maan lijiye ek rope do pegs A aur B ke beech khinchi hai, aur aapko wo point chahiye jo ise kisi ratio mein baante, jaise A se two to three. section formula yahi nikaalta hai.
har coordinate mein alag-alag, dividing point dono endpoints ka weighted average hai. aur sabse zaroori — wahi same weights x, y aur z teenon par ek saath lagte hain.
yahaan internal section formula hai. A B ko m to n ratio mein, A se naapte hue, baantne wala point har coordinate mein yahii weighted average hai, denominator m plus n ke saath.

weighted average kyon? Agar point B ke kareeb baitha hai, to use B ke coordinates zyada milne chahiye, isliye bhaari weight us endpoint par baithta hai jiske aap kareeb hain. Ye intuition weights ko galat ends par lagane se bachati hai.
safe tarika: ratio ke pehle hisse wala weight, m, far endpoint x two ko multiply karta hai, aur n near endpoint x one ko.
External division ek hi sign flip karta hai. n ki jagah minus n rakhiye, aur numerator tatha denominator dono plus se minus ho jate hain. ye tab use hota hai jab dividing point segment ke bahar ho.
Midpoint bas sabse simple case hai, equal weights one to one ke saath. ye endpoints ke plain average mein badal jata hai.

Midpoint ko apna sanity check banaiye. Jab bhi koi section formula ka answer shak paida kare, puchhiye ki equal weights ise beech mein late ya nahi — agar numbers sahi taraf nahi jhuk rahe, to aapne koi weight swap kar diya hai.
chaliye foundation formulas ko ek board par ikattha karte hain, taaki solve shuru karne se pehle aap inhen saath-saath dekh sakein.
do points ke beech distance — squared coordinate differences ke sum ka root.
m to n ratio mein internal division, har coordinate par, numerator aur denominator mein plus ke saath.
External division — wahi shape minus ke saath, jo n ki jagah minus n rakhne se aata hai.
Midpoint bas har coordinate mein endpoints ka average hai.
Centroid — vertices ka average, triangle ke liye teen se aur tetrahedron ke liye chaar se divide karte hue.
Volume scalar triple product ka one sixth hai; area cross product magnitude ka half. Dono modulus rakhte hain kyunki ye sizes hain.
aur axis tatha plane distances: x axis se root y squared plus z squared; y z plane se x ka size. baakiyon ke liye coordinates cycle kar dijiye.
chaliye is subtopic ke formulas ikattha kar lete hain, isse pehle ki hum inse problems solve karein.
Master identity — direction cosines ke squares one mein jodte hain.
ek upyogi bonus identity jo seedhe nikalti hai: teenon angles ke sines ke squares two mein judte hain.
Direction ratios ko direction cosines mein badalne ke liye, ratio triple ki length se divide kijiye, ek shared plus ya minus ke saath.
do points se guzarti line ke liye, direction ratios bas coordinate differences hain.
Line ka vector form — ek fixed point plus lambda times direction.
aur Cartesian symmetric form, direction ratios denominators ke roop mein aur point constants ke roop mein.
chaliye angle aur shortest distance ke formulas ikattha kar lete hain, isse pehle ki hum inse solve karein.
Acute angle: dono directions ka sign hataaya hua, normalised overlap. Agar aapko direction cosines diye hon, denominator one hai aur ye bas dot product ka modulus hai.
do quick tests: perpendicular ke liye dot product zero, parallel ke liye proportional ratios.
Skew shortest distance vector form mein — volume, base area se divide kiya hua.
Cartesian determinant form bas wahi cheez hai coordinate dar coordinate likhi hui: triple product determinant hai, aur denominator cross product ka size.

aur do aur: coplanarity condition, triple product barabar zero, jo shortest distance ka numerator bhi hai; aur parallel line distance, shared direction ka joining vector ke saath cross, direction ke size se divide.

Choice par ek aakhiri baat: vectors, ratios aur cosines mein angle ke expressions sab ek hi baat kahte hain, to jo aapke diye data se match kare wahi uthaiye. shortest distance ke liye bhi wahi — vectors diye hon to vector form, symmetric equations diye hon to determinant form.
aath alag cheezen yaad karne ke bajay, har case ke liye do sawalon par tikiye: perpendicular kahaan land karta hai, aur wo kitna lamba hai. image tab hamesha twice the foot minus the point hota hai.
Line ke liye, foot parameter lambda nought hai A P ka b par projection, b ke size ke square par, aur foot hai a plus lambda nought b.
Line distance hai cross product magnitude over b ka size, aur image hai twice the foot minus the point.
Plane ke liye, single number t hai point par plane expression, normal ke size ke square par.
Foot hai point minus t times normal, image minus two t times normal, aur distance hai plane expression over normal ki length.

ek fark tez rakhiye: t normal ke size ke square se divide hota hai, kyunki ye vector ko plane tak pahunchane ke liye scale karta hai, jabki distance normal ke size se divide hoti hai, kyunki wo us step ko pure length mein badalti hai.
to sab kuch foot par tikaiye. jaise hi wo mil jaaye, distance point se foot tak ki length hai, aur image hai twice the foot minus the point — wo aakhri identity line aur plane dono ke liye ek hi hai.

ye constructions varied dikhte hain, par ye sawaal ke hisaab se vyavasthit hain, nai theory nahin. intersections ke liye substitute karke solve; planes ke liye normal banao; bisectors ke liye normalise karke equate.
Line versus plane: dot product non zero ka matlab wo cross karti hai, to lambda ke liye solve; dot product zero ka matlab lies in ko parallel se alag karne ke liye ek point test.

Plane banana: normal hai intersecting lines ke liye dono directions ka cross, line and point ke liye direction ka point tak ke vector ke saath cross, ya parallel lines ke liye direction ka joining vector ke saath cross.
Bisector planes: pehla plane expression uske normal ki length par barabar plus ya minus doosra uske normal ki length par. do perpendicular bisectors.

kisi line ko reflect karne ke liye, intersection point M rakhiye, koi doosra point Q ko Q dash par reflect kijiye, aur M aur Q dash ko jodiye. projection diye plane ka us plane ke saath intersection hai jo line se guzre aur uske perpendicular ho.

ekjut karne wala move: kisi bhi line plane kaam se pehle, b dot n nikaaliye. non zero aur wo cross karti hai; zero aur aap ek point test karte hain. wo single number bata deta hai aap teenon configurations mein se kismein hain aur isliye kaun si method lagani hai.

aur dhyan dijiye reflection aur projection koi naya formula nahi jodte. wo perpendicular toolkit dobaara use karte hain — ek fixed intersection point plus ek reflected point, ya shadow line mein judi do perpendicular feet.
yahaan poore chapter ke liye aapka complete toolkit hai — ek board jo har load bearing formula dobaara batata hai. yahaan kuch naya nahin, bas exam se pehle ek tez aakhri sweep.

Direction cosines ke liye, master identity, aur direction ratios se conversion unki length se divide karke.
kisi line ke vector aur Cartesian equations — ek point plus ek direction.
do lines ke beech acute angle, aur skew shortest distance volume over base area ke roop mein.
Planes ke liye, point normal equation, plane to plane angle normals ke cosine se, aur line to plane angle sine se — plane to plane cosine, line to plane sine.
Point to plane distance, aur line of intersection se guzarti planes ki family.
aur perpendicular toolkit: point line distance b ke size par, aur plane ke liye single number t, image point se two t normals door. yahi poora chapter ek board mein.
aakhir mein, quick recall box — vo one line reminders jo exam pressure mein sabse common slips pakadte hain. har problem shuru karne se pehle har ek ko khud se boliye.

kisi axis se distance shared coordinate chhodti hai aur root ke neeche do rakhti hai; kisi plane se distance sirf wo ek zero wala coordinate rakhti hai. in dono ko kabhi gaddamadd mat kijiye.

Directions ke liye: direction cosines squares mein kul one kharch karte hain; ratios ek recipe hain aur cosines tayaar dish, to hamesha normalise kijiye; aur Cartesian equation ke ratios padhne se pehle use standardise kijiye.

Lines ke liye: cross product skew lines ko bridge karta hai aur dot product uske saath project karta hai; acute value ke liye angle numerator ko modulus mein lapetie; aur zero scalar triple product ka matlab lines coplanar hain aur milti hain.

Planes ke liye: plane to plane cosine use karta hai, line to plane sine — topic ki sabse common galti. Aur lagbhag har plane sawaal normal dhoondho mein ghat jata hai; forms, angles aur distances sab usi se behte hain.

aur perpendicular toolkit tatha configurations ke liye: foot ke liye dot, gap ke liye cross; foot midpoint hai, to image hai twice the foot minus the point; dot product b dot n cross versus parallel tay karta hai; aur bisect karne ke liye, normalise karke plus ya minus lijiye. yahi chapter eleven ke liye aapka complete quick recall hai.

External division — wahi shape minus ke saath, jo n ki jagah minus n rakhne se aata hai.
Midpoint bas har coordinate mein endpoints ka average hai.
Centroid — vertices ka average, triangle ke liye teen se aur tetrahedron ke liye chaar se divide karte hue.
Volume scalar triple product ka one sixth hai; area cross product magnitude ka half. Dono modulus rakhte hain kyunki ye sizes hain.
aur axis tatha plane distances: x axis se root y squared plus z squared; y z plane se x ka size. baakiyon ke liye coordinates cycle kar dijiye.
chaliye is subtopic ke formulas ikattha kar lete hain, isse pehle ki hum inse problems solve karein.
Master identity — direction cosines ke squares one mein jodte hain.
ek upyogi bonus identity jo seedhe nikalti hai: teenon angles ke sines ke squares two mein judte hain.
Direction ratios ko direction cosines mein badalne ke liye, ratio triple ki length se divide kijiye, ek shared plus ya minus ke saath.
do points se guzarti line ke liye, direction ratios bas coordinate differences hain.
Line ka vector form — ek fixed point plus lambda times direction.
aur Cartesian symmetric form, direction ratios denominators ke roop mein aur point constants ke roop mein.
chaliye angle aur shortest distance ke formulas ikattha kar lete hain, isse pehle ki hum inse solve karein.
Acute angle: dono directions ka sign hataaya hua, normalised overlap. Agar aapko direction cosines diye hon, denominator one hai aur ye bas dot product ka modulus hai.
do quick tests: perpendicular ke liye dot product zero, parallel ke liye proportional ratios.
Skew shortest distance vector form mein — volume, base area se divide kiya hua.
Cartesian determinant form bas wahi cheez hai coordinate dar coordinate likhi hui: triple product determinant hai, aur denominator cross product ka size.

aur do aur: coplanarity condition, triple product barabar zero, jo shortest distance ka numerator bhi hai; aur parallel line distance, shared direction ka joining vector ke saath cross, direction ke size se divide.

Choice par ek aakhiri baat: vectors, ratios aur cosines mein angle ke expressions sab ek hi baat kahte hain, to jo aapke diye data se match kare wahi uthaiye. shortest distance ke liye bhi wahi — vectors diye hon to vector form, symmetric equations diye hon to determinant form.
aath alag cheezen yaad karne ke bajay, har case ke liye do sawalon par tikiye: perpendicular kahaan land karta hai, aur wo kitna lamba hai. image tab hamesha twice the foot minus the point hota hai.
Line ke liye, foot parameter lambda nought hai A P ka b par projection, b ke size ke square par, aur foot hai a plus lambda nought b.
Line distance hai cross product magnitude over b ka size, aur image hai twice the foot minus the point.
Plane ke liye, single number t hai point par plane expression, normal ke size ke square par.
Foot hai point minus t times normal, image minus two t times normal, aur distance hai plane expression over normal ki length.

ek fark tez rakhiye: t normal ke size ke square se divide hota hai, kyunki ye vector ko plane tak pahunchane ke liye scale karta hai, jabki distance normal ke size se divide hoti hai, kyunki wo us step ko pure length mein badalti hai.
to sab kuch foot par tikaiye. jaise hi wo mil jaye, distance point se foot tak ki length hai, aur image hai twice the foot minus the point — wo aakhri identity line aur plane dono ke liye ek hi hai.

ye constructions varied dikhte hain, par ye sawaal ke hisaab se vyavasthit hain, nai theory nahin. intersections ke liye substitute karke solve; planes ke liye normal banao; bisectors ke liye normalise karke equate.
Line versus plane: dot product non zero ka matlab wo cross karti hai, to lambda ke liye solve; dot product zero ka matlab lies in ko parallel se alag karne ke liye ek point test.

Plane banana: normal hai intersecting lines ke liye dono directions ka cross, line and point ke liye direction ka point tak ke vector ke saath cross, ya parallel lines ke liye direction ka joining vector ke saath cross.
Bisector planes: pehla plane expression uske normal ki length par barabar plus ya minus doosra uske normal ki length par. do perpendicular bisectors.

kisi line ko reflect karne ke liye, intersection point M rakhiye, koi doosra point Q ko Q dash par reflect kijiye, aur M aur Q dash ko jodiye. projection diye plane ka us plane ke saath intersection hai jo line se guzre aur uske perpendicular ho.

ekjut karne wala move: kisi bhi line plane kaam se pehle, b dot n nikaaliye. non zero aur wo cross karti hai; zero aur aap ek point test karte hain. wo single number bata deta hai aap teenon configurations mein se kismein hain aur isliye kaun si method lagani hai.

aur dhyan dijiye reflection aur projection koi naya formula nahi jodte. wo perpendicular toolkit dobaara use karte hain — ek fixed intersection point plus ek reflected point, ya shadow line mein judi do perpendicular feet.

Point to plane distance, aur line of intersection se guzarti planes ki family.

Foundations se: distance Pythagoras do baar hai; section formula mein far weight pehle naamit hisse par baithta hai; aur negative ratio ka matlab external division, segment ke baahar.
kisi axis se distance shared coordinate chhodti hai aur root ke neeche do rakhti hai; kisi plane se distance sirf wo ek zero wala coordinate rakhti hai. in dono ko kabhi gaddamadd mat kijiye.

Directions ke liye: direction cosines squares mein kul one kharch karte hain; ratios ek recipe hain aur cosines tayaar dish, to hamesha normalise kijiye; aur Cartesian equation ke ratios padhne se pehle use standardise kijiye.

Lines ke liye: cross product skew lines ko bridge karta hai aur dot product uske saath project karta hai; acute value ke liye angle numerator ko modulus mein lapetiyega; aur zero scalar triple product ka matlab lines coplanar hain aur milti hain.

Planes ke liye: plane to plane cosine use karta hai, line to plane sine — topic ki sabse common galti. Aur lagbhag har plane sawaal normal dhoondho mein ghat jata hai; forms, angles aur distances sab usi se behte hain.

aur perpendicular toolkit tatha configurations ke liye: foot ke liye dot, gap ke liye cross; foot midpoint hai, to image hai twice the foot minus the point; dot product b dot n cross versus parallel tay karta hai; aur bisect karne ke liye, normalise karke plus ya minus lijiye. yahi chapter eleven ke liye aapka complete quick recall hai.
